newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco appoints director for Somaca car firm.
newsitem.headline: Morocco appoints director for Somaca car firm.

text.p: Morocco has appointed Ali Ghannam as managing director for the country's leading car assembly firm, Societe Marocaine de Constructions Automobiles (SOMACA), the Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
Ghannam, 38, who replaced Mehdi Benbouchta, is a senior official in charge of Morocco's industrial sector at the trade ministry.
Established in Casablanca in 1959, SOMACA has a capital of 60 million dirhams ($6.9 million) and a total capacity of 25,000 vehicles per year.
"SOMACA should be ambitious and integrate the international car market...Therefore the firm should upgrade its capacity and productivity future," the ministry said.
The appointment coincided with the government decision to boost the output of the "economic car", Mohamed Mekouar, a market analyst at Upline Securities, said.
A version of the Italian Fiat Uno, the economic car was produced by SOMACA's plant assembler and marketed through 10 points of sale since September 1995, Mekouar said.
The trade ministry forecasts 15,000 will be sold on the domestic market by end 1996, officials said.

"This is still below the 50,000 cars that Fiat wishes to sell in a three-year period...The Moroccan government and Italian manufacturer defined a set of actions to improve the current number," the analyst added.
SOMACA is not listed on the Casablanca stock market.
